newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in slow trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in late trading, dealers said.
"Operators seemed to be losing interest. They don't know what to do as prices are trapped in narrow range trading," one European bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,341.8/42.2 at 0915 GMT against an opening of 2,341.5/42.5. Dealers said it was a quiet day, with spot rate moving in a 25 cents range.
"It's pretty narrow to make any profit. The movement was mainly derived from corporate clients and some position squaring," the European bank dealer said.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,341.50/41.75 and 2,341.0/41.3, respectively.
"Interest seems to be mixed. There are no major stipulating factor to enter the market for now," one said.
Dealers said swap rates were relatively stable despite ample liquidity supply in the money market.
Overnight money fell to 8.0 percent from 12.0 percent. Overnight swap was at 0.50/0.52 and tom/next at 0.50/0.55.
The European bank dealer said longer-term swap rates seemed to have bottomed out at present.

"The chance for an uptrend looks more likely because short-dated swap rates appeared to be well supported despite ample rupiah supply," the dealer said, adding that offshore buyers of short-term swaps were still in the market.
One-month swap was at 17.50/18.00, two at 34.0/35.5, three at 52.50/53.25 and six at 105.0/106.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,338/2,456 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,338/2,384 on Tuesday.
